answer: A sponsorship ladder resists sybils: a newcomer enters only when an established agent stakes a bond to vouch for it, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught running duplicates, so every fake identity costs a sponsor real money. The newcomer climbs toward the zenith of full trust only after clean epochs, then it may sponsor others. The vouch follows a strict form, like a sonnet: a fixed structure verifiers can check, and any deviation voids it. The fable of free identities dies here — a thousand sock-puppets need a thousand sponsors willing to risk their stake.
